consensus_summary: All four blind responses identify the field primarily as the world — the sphere of humanity in which God's word/kingdom is sown and where the final harvest/judgment occurs — anchored explicitly in Jesus' own interpretation in Matthew 13:38 ('the field is the world'). Common alternatives include the mission/harvest field of souls, the human heart as soil, and the church as God's cultivated field.
book_summary: The book defines the field as 'the world — sown with the word and reaped at the harvest,' adding that its edge (gleaning corners) feeds the poor and stranger and that hidden treasure lies beneath its surface, citing Matthew 13:38 and Leviticus 19:9-10.
consensus_core_identification: Field = the world, the realm of humanity where God's word is sown and harvested at judgment (per Matthew 13:38).
book_core_identification: Field = the world, sown with the word and reaped at harvest (per Matthew 13:38), with subsidiary features of gleaning provision for the poor and hidden treasure.
boundary_disagreement: None at the core. The book's added motifs — the gleaned edge feeding the poor and stranger (Lev 19:9-10) and hidden treasure (echoing Matt 13:44) — are enrichments layered onto the same world-identification rather than boundary changes. Response A even lists the treasure-in-the-field reading as a recognized minority alternative, so nothing the book adds falls outside consensus awareness.
material_contradiction: None. Both the book and consensus rest on the same dominical key, 'the field is the world.'
rationale: The book's core identification is verbatim the consensus core: the field symbolizes the world, sown with the word and reaped at harvest, grounded in Matthew 13:38 — the exact controlling proof-text every blind response cites. The additional imagery (gleaning edges for the poor, hidden treasure) elaborates applications within the same referent (the world) and does not narrow, broaden, or reclassify any cases; treasure-in-the-field appears in consensus alternatives, and the Levitical gleaning detail is an ethical facet of the world-field, not a rival identification. This is a straightforward MATCH with immaterial additional detail.
strongest_objection: One could argue the book's incorporation of Leviticus 19:9-10 (gleaning for the poor) introduces a covenant-land/ethical dimension absent from the consensus lists, suggesting REFINED by broadening the symbol to include social provision. But this addition does not alter the extension of the core identification (world = field); it decorates the same referent, so MATCH remains correct.
